task.description:
REWORK 1 of the ISS-0440 fix design. CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR returned FAIL with two BLOCKERs and one MINOR. Read its handoff (artifacts_in[0]) in full. Items 5 and 6 (additive/default-preserving; AC3/AC4/AC5) PASSED and are settled -- do not revisit them. The autofix refusal contract was also verified correct on item 2; only its stated PREMISE was wrong.

BLOCKER 1 -- OVERCLAIMED UNAVOIDABILITY (item 1). Your design says of Mechanism B that 'there is no path through this procedure that reaches step 4 without having passed step 2.' The validator established that is not literally true: HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md 1.3 is itself PROSE -- ORCH manually remembering to git add && git commit, pointed at from ORCHESTRATOR.md:23's MUST list -- not anything code-enforced. Its good track record (docs/anti-patterns.md:1123 records the single incident that CAUSED 1.3 to be written, with no logged recurrence since) is evidence of RELIABILITY, not of structural guarantee. The validator also found that main's squash-merge history makes 1.3 compliance unverifiable from main directly -- an 88.5% single-commit figure it first measured turned out to be a squash artifact -- though this run's own unsquashed branch does show the real two-commit dispatch-then-complete pattern live (45ac032a dispatch -> dc7431b9 completion).
   REQUIRED FIX: state plainly that Mechanism B inherits 1.3's RELIABILITY CLASS (strong track record, procedurally enforced, NOT code-guaranteed) rather than implying CI-gate-strength unavoidability. Keep Mechanism B -- it is not being rejected; the validator faulted the CLAIM, not the mechanism. Then, because the whole issue is that six prose mitigations failed, ADDRESS THE CONSEQUENCE HONESTLY: given B is procedural, what carries the actual structural guarantee? If the answer is 'Mechanism A alone, at CI', say so explicitly and explain why the pair is still worth having (B is a latency improvement over A, not an independent guarantee). ORCH's own view, which you may adopt or reject with reasoning: a design that is honest about being 'CI-guaranteed plus a procedural early-catch' is ACCEPTABLE and materially better than the six prose-only predecessors, because A genuinely cannot be skipped -- but it must not be SOLD as more than that, since overclaiming is precisely how a seventh mitigation becomes an eighth tally line.

BLOCKER 2 -- THE AC1 DEMONSTRATION CANNOT EXECUTE AS WRITTEN (item 4). Your section 5 has ELIXIR-DEV plant a bad status in a scratch fixture OUTSIDE handoffs/, then run `mix letflow.lint_handoffs` against it. That cannot work: run/1 (line 234) calls handoff_files() with NO argument, and the default is the hardcoded @handoffs_dir 'handoffs' (line 97), so a fixture outside handoffs/ is INVISIBLE to any real CLI invocation. AC1 requires a demonstration by a REAL RUN with actual output quoted, so a plan the CLI cannot execute fails AC1 outright.
   GOOD NEWS, and ORCH verified this from source so you can build on it: handoff_files/1 at line 279 ALREADY takes a dir parameter with a default -- `def handoff_files(dir \ @handoffs_dir)`. The capability exists; it is simply not reachable from the CLI because run/1 does not pass anything through. So the fix is small: specify how run/1 exposes a directory override (e.g. a --dir flag parsed from args, defaulting to @handoffs_dir so CI's no-flag invocation is byte-identical in behaviour). Design that override explicitly, state its default, and confirm it cannot change the no-flag path CI depends on. Alternatively, if you prefer the fixture to live INSIDE handoffs/ under a scratch run-id, address the obvious hazard: a deliberately-bad handoff committed under handoffs/ would be linted by every OTHER host's CI too and would break their builds -- so if you go that way, the fixture must never be committed, and you must say how that is guaranteed.

MINOR -- CORRECT A FALSE PREMISE ORCH SUPPLIED (item 2). ORCH's dispatch told you a null-status handoff exists today; that was WRONG and the validator caught it. ORCH's original scan used a broad glob (handoffs/**/*.json) rather than the linter's own discovery pattern. Re-scanned with the linter's actual pattern (handoffs/**/step*.*): 1900 files, ZERO bad, missing, null, or non-string top-level status values. The file ORCH cited is not even discovered by handoff_files/0 (wrong basename) and its null field was the unrelated result.status. Correct any design text resting on that premise. Your autofix refusal contract was verified CORRECT and is unchanged -- but since null/missing is now known NOT to occur in the corpus, state what autofix does on it anyway (defensively refusing is fine); do not silently leave the path unspecified just because it is currently unpopulated.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE: change nothing else. Both mechanisms keep their shape, the four-option verdicts stand, the hook rejection stands, AC3/AC4/AC5 stand. Design only, no implementation code. Update lib/letflow/design/iss440-handoff-status-enforcement.md in place, complete this handoff, commit both to branch feature/WF03-ISS0440-20260903. rework_count 1 of max 3.

result.summary:
All three rework findings addressed in lib/letflow/design/iss440-handoff-status-enforcement.md, in place, scope otherwise unchanged (both mechanisms keep their shape, four-option verdicts and hook rejection stand, AC3/AC4/AC5 stand).

BLOCKER 1 (overclaimed unavoidability): withdrew the false claim 'there is no path through this procedure that reaches step 4 without having passed step 2' from section 3.2 -- stated explicitly it is not literally true. New section 0 addendum distinguishes structural (code/infrastructure-enforced, section 1.1's CI gate) from procedural (documented-MUST, section 1.2's ORCH dispatch commit) unavoidability up front, so the two mechanisms are never presented as the same strength of guarantee. Rewrote section 1.2 in full: states HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md 1.3 is prose ORCH executes, not code-enforced; cites the anti-patterns.md:1123 incident that caused 1.3 to be written and its clean record since; cites this run's own unsquashed branch (45ac032a dispatch -> dc7431b9 completion) as the live two-commit evidence CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR itself surfaced, and notes why main's squash-merge history is the wrong place to verify this (the apparent single-commit figure there is a squash artifact). New section 3.5 ('Where the actual structural guarantee lives, stated honestly') draws the required consequence: only Mechanism A carries the structural guarantee; if Mechanism B were ever silently dropped, Mechanism A still catches every violation at CI, before merge; Mechanism B's honest value is a free latency improvement on the common path, not a second independent guarantee. Adopted ORCH's own framing verbatim as the design's self-description ('CI-guaranteed plus a procedural early-catch') and stated explicitly why it is not sold as more than that. AC1's two-catches framing and section 6.2/7 item 2-3 reworded to match this precision throughout -- grepped the whole file afterward for every remaining 'unavoidable'/'structurally impossible'/'no path through' occurrence and confirmed each now reads at the corrected strength.

BLOCKER 2 (AC1 demonstration unexecutable): added a --dir <path> flag to run/1 alongside --autofix (section 2.1, new), threading straight into handoff_files/1's already-parameterized dir argument (verified at line 279) instead of the hardcoded zero-arg handoff_files() call run/1 makes today. Specified resolve_dir/1's exact no-flag behaviour (returns @handoffs_dir unchanged, byte-identical to today's hardcoded default) and stated explicitly why CI's own invocation (mix letflow.check's alias entry, no arguments appended) cannot be affected by this addition. Rewrote the AC1 demonstration in section 5 end to end: fixture now lives outside handoffs/ (scratch/iss440-fixtures/ or test/fixtures/), invoked via --dir so a real mix letflow.lint_handoffs --dir <fixture-dir> [--autofix] run actually sees it -- quoted-output steps for the PASS-fixture catch, the --autofix correction, the FAIL-fixture refusal, and a new step 5 confirming the no-flag path still scans only the real handoffs/ corpus (proving --dir's addition changed nothing about CI's behaviour). Also named and rejected the inside-handoffs/ alternative explicitly, stating the hazard (any other host's CI would lint a committed bad-status fixture and break their builds) rather than silently choosing between the two options.

MINOR (false null-status premise): corrected section 2.5 to state the rescanned, corrected figure (1900 files via the linter's own handoffs/**/step*.* pattern, zero bad/missing/null/non-string top-level status values) in place of the original 1899-file claim, and to explain why the original scan's finding was wrong (broad glob instead of the linter's own discovery pattern; the cited file isn't matched by handoff_files/1 at all; its null field was the unrelated result.status). Added an explicit statement that a missing/non-string top-level status is refused identically to FAIL under --autofix (section 2.2's mapping table already had this row; section 2.5 now restates it with the reporting-message distinction -- the refusal reason names the actual condition found rather than reusing FAIL's ambiguity wording) even though the corpus shows zero occurrences today, and points at check_h1_status/2's own existing missing-vs-mismatch clause split (verified lines 411-435) as the precedent this mirrors, so the path is specified rather than left implicit because it is currently unpopulated.

Verified no implementation code was introduced by any of these edits: grepped the full file for elixir/ex code fences and def/defp patterns after all changes -- none present; only @spec-style signatures, closed data-shape tables/maps, and numbered procedure prose.
